content.title: Block transfer initiation for frozen_user
content.intent: Prove that the frozen persona cannot perform transfers through ordinary UI actions.
content.technique_notes: Applied auth/permission, negative, and state/flow techniques because the PRD states the frozen persona has an explicit 'no transfers' restriction and that this restriction must not be bypassable through ordinary UI actions. Risk-gated interaction strength was 3 because money, auth, and data-loss apply, but no covering array was needed because this scenario fixes a single persona-state path.

content.title: Complete a supported transfer between two eligible accounts as standard_user
content.intent: Prove that a permitted authenticated user can complete a supported transfer and see consistent balance and history updates.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning and state/flow techniques for the normal permitted transfer path: authenticated standard_user, distinct eligible accounts, and a valid positive amount accepted by the product. Risk-gated interaction strength was 3 because money, auth, and data-loss apply, but no covering array was needed because this scenario uses one representative allowed combination rather than sweeping multiple independent classes.

parameters.amount_class: valid positive amount accepted by the application

content.title: Reject a zero transfer amount
content.intent: Prove that a non-positive boundary amount is not silently accepted as a successful transfer.
content.technique_notes: Applied boundary value analysis at the documented positivity boundary and negative/error technique because the PRD states invalid monetary values must not be silently accepted and transfer amounts must comply with positivity constraints. Risk-gated interaction strength was 3 because money and data-loss apply, degraded in practice to a single boundary input because only the amount boundary is under test here.

content.title: Reject a non-numeric transfer amount
content.intent: Prove that an invalid formatted amount is not silently accepted as a successful transfer.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning over invalid monetary input classes and negative/error technique because the PRD requires monetary inputs to obey numeric and formatting rules. Risk-gated interaction strength was 3 because money and data-loss apply, but the scenario intentionally isolates one invalid input class rather than combining unrelated variables.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Ranked first because bypassing the frozen-user restriction would be an auth failure on a money-moving action and the PRD explicitly calls out this persona restriction.
[value_score] Ranked second because the successful transfer path proves the core value of the use case and covers balance/history integrity on committed movement.
[value_score] Ranked third because the zero-amount boundary is explicitly implied by the positivity rule and is a common financial validation defect.
[value_score] Ranked fourth because invalid-format rejection is important, but it is less business-critical than permission bypass or committed-state integrity.
